one_month_reasoning: Q3 2026 earnings fall inside the window. The date is not yet confirmed; MarketBeat estimates 2026-10-26, after the close. The Q3 guide is $1.595-1.625B revenue and $2.01-2.07 non-GAAP EPS, against consensus of $2.04 and $1.61B. With a record $8.1B backlog and beat-and-raise quarters in Q1 and Q2, a modest beat is the likely outcome. The first FY2027 commentary is the swing factor: FY2027 consensus revenue growth is only about 13%. I am correcting a round-1 fact: Synopsys did not fall after its August beat. It closed up 13.4% the next day ($410 to $464.89, Twelve Data), so EDA beats have recently been rewarded. Against that, CDNS has just rallied 28% in 12 sessions, from a $273.96 close on Sep 15 to $350.75, including +6.2% on Oct 1 on thin volume. That is far more than my round-1 note of a bounce from about $305, and it raises the odds of some short-term giveback. Headline risk from AI disruption is real: CDNS fell 9.5% on 2026-07-17 on the Kimi K3 demo. Net: median about $350, close to spot, with the earnings-beat drift and the post-rally reversal roughly cancelling. I use a lognormal sigma of 0.13, a bit above the 11.7% from annual vol / 3.5, to cover the earnings gap and the recent volatility.

fair_value.method: 60% P/E: NTM non-GAAP EPS at Oct-2027 of about $10.60 (25% of FY2027 consensus $9.55, 75% of FY2028 at $10.98) x 35x = $371. 40% forward FCF yield: NTM FCF of about $2.37B at a 2.4% yield = $98.8B EV, less $1.06B net debt, over 274M shares = $357. Blended = $365.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: NTM non-GAAP EPS at 2027-10-01 of $10.60 x 35x

inputs_detail.derivation: Two independent aggregators agree: StockAnalysis $9.56 (26 analysts) and Zacks about $9.54. This replaces the round-1 $9.50, which was an unverified secondary figure nudged up. It is supported by Hexagon D&E turning accretive in 2027 (source 8).
This corrects my round-1 assumption that 18-20% growth continues into 2027. The Street has 2027 decelerating as the Hexagon contribution laps.

FY2027 $9.55 x 1.15. That is about 13% revenue growth (the consensus 2027 pace and SemiAnalysis's 13% EDA CAGR), plus modest operating leverage, plus about 1% a year net share reduction from buybacks of about 50% of FCF. It gives no credit for agentic revenue; Tech Fund argues that could lift growth to the mid-20s.

Today the stock is about 38x NTM EPS ($350.73 / about $9.19). It troughed near 30x at the Sep-15 low ($273.96), and R Fund cites 33x at $280. TIKR cited about 41x NTM in July before the Kimi drop, and Zacks put the forward P/E at 36.3x on Sep 22 at $302.60. I use 35x, slightly below today's level, because a recurring AI-disruption discount now looks embedded (two roughly 9-10% single-day drops in 2026) and 2027 growth slows to about 13%.

methods.name: FCF yield
methods.inputs: NTM FCF at horizon about $2.37B / 2.4% = $98.8B EV; less $1.06B net debt; 274M shares

inputs_detail.derivation: $2.0B OCF less about $0.15B capex (historical run-rate; capex is not guided in the CFO commentary).
Grown about 15% a year, in line with the consensus EPS growth path (FY2027 EPS +17.5%, revenue +13%). Lowered from round-1's 18% a year after verifying the 2027 revenue consensus.
The Hexagon D&E deal closed on 2026-02-23 (source 8), so it is already in the Q2 balance sheet; no pending cash outflow.
Q2 diluted count of 276.2M and FY2026 guide of 275.5-277.5M, less about 1% from buybacks of about $200M a quarter.

The current price implies about 2.2% on FY2027 FCF (about $97B EV / $2.13B). The Sep-15 low implied about 2.8%. I use 2.4%, between the two, as a no-re-rating level with a modest AI-disruption discount.

bear.story: The AI-disruption narrative hardens: another Kimi-style open-source or agentic demo moves closer to advanced nodes, ChipAgents-type startups (120+ deployments) win budget, or seat growth visibly slows. A hyperscaler capex pause or renewed China EDA licensing curbs (15% of revenue) adds to it. FY2027 EPS growth drops to about 10% (about $9.0 NTM falls to roughly $9.6 at the horizon), and the multiple sits at about 26x, below the Sep-15 trough of about 30x.

base.story: FY2027 plays out near consensus (about 13% revenue growth, $9.55 EPS) with a small agentic contribution. Backlog stays above $8B and the multiple settles at 35-36x on NTM EPS of about $10.60.

bull.story: Agentic products (20+ ChipStack and 25+ ViraStack customer projects) turn into priced consumption revenue visible in FY2027 guidance. The Mizuho and Tech Fund agentic-engineer TAM thesis gains acceptance, the 2027 hyperscaler capex build ($1.1-1.3T) keeps AI design starts high, and the stock re-rates to about 43x on NTM EPS of about $11.4.

thesis_break_reason: In September the stock fell to $273.96 with no change in fundamentals, and the 52-week low is $262.75, so sentiment alone can push it into the $260s-270s. Below about $245 it would trade near 25-26x FY2027 consensus EPS, about 7% under the 52-week low. That level most likely means the market sees real fundamental damage: a backlog decline or weak first FY2027 guidance in February, evidence that agentic or open-source flows are taking spend at leading-edge nodes (not just 45nm demos), new China EDA export licensing, or a hyperscaler capex cut.

Startup competition in verification: ChipAgents grew ARR 6x in 1H26 with 120+ deployments and $134M raised, and Cognichip has raised $93M. Small today, but they compete in the very workflow where Cadence touts its 40x speedups.
Multiple durability: the stock went from about $365 to $273.96 and back to $350.75 within about 2.5 months, largely on sentiment.
FY2027 growth: consensus implies about 13% revenue growth versus 18-20% in 2026. The February guide sets the tone.

Hiring signals are mixed: Revelio shows the hiring pace slowing, while TrueUp shows about 919 open jobs and no recorded layoffs (Sep 2026). The round-1 claim of a 4% reduction remains unconfirmed, so I drop it.
reasoning: Continuation of round 1 with about 25 more searches and page reads. The main changes: (1) Verified consensus. Two aggregators give FY2027 EPS of $9.55 (StockAnalysis $9.56, Zacks about $9.54), but FY2027 revenue consensus is only about +13% ($7.17B), not the 18-20% I had assumed carried over. That lowers my FY2028 growth path and the FCF growth to about 15%. (2) Price history corrected from Twelve Data: the September low was $273.96 on Sep 15 (not about $305), followed by a 28% rally to $350.75, partly on an expanded TSMC collaboration and the RTL Generation Agent launch. Synopsys rose 13.4% after its August beat, the opposite of what round 1 said. (3) A bear-case signal I had missed: on 2026-07-17 Moonshot's Kimi K3 designed a 45nm chip in 48 hours using only open-source EDA, and CDNS fell 9.5% in a day. This is confirmed across an X post, the SemiWiki thread and TIKR. Practitioners on SemiWiki mostly dismissed it (old node, no yield data), and Mizuho and BNP called it a buying opportunity, but it shows the stock carries a recurring AI-disruption discount. Agentic startups are also scaling (ChipAgents: $134M raised, 120+ deployments). (4) Bull evidence: Devgan says agents are priced roughly at the value of a human engineer's work on a consumption-plus-subscription model, and customers keep buying the base tools. Tech Fund cites about $25-50k per agent and argues Street numbers give no credit for it. The 2027 hyperscaler capex outlook ($1.1-1.3T) supports AI design starts. Fair value moves down from $378 to $365 (P/E 35x on $10.60 = $371; 2.4% yield on NTM FCF of $2.37B = $357). That is about 4% above spot and below the roughly $404-405 average analyst target. Scenarios of $250/$375/$490 at 25/50/25 give a mean of about $372. The ladder is a 92/8 mixture: a lognormal with median $365 and sigma 0.34, plus a disruption-tail lognormal with median $250 and sigma 0.40. The overall median is about $354, with a fatter left tail than round 1, and the effective dispersion sits a little under the 41% realized vol because backlog and about 80% recurring revenue cap fundamental dispersion. Remaining limits: X is not fetchable (the social signal comes via search results), Alpha Vantage was rate-limited and the Twelve Data estimates endpoint was unavailable on this plan, the TrueUp and Simply Wall St pages blocked fetching, and I found no prediction market on EDA export controls.
